messages:
li: kicking off canary upgrade for us-west-2-gpu-ng-canary — AMI bump + kubelet 1.25->1.26 via terraform. apply in progress, will tail CNI and kube-proxy. :eyes:
ops-bot: terraform apply started by li (run id tf-run-2026-03-18-09). plan shows nodegroup will replace 1 of 3 instances.
sam: are we doing graceful drain/maxUnavailable=1 on the nodegroup? last time drain timing caused pods to pile up.
li: yes, update_config in TF is set to { max_unavailable = 1 }. snippet:
```
resource "aws_eks_node_group" "gpu" {
  update_config { max_unavailable = 1 }
  launch_template { id = aws_launch_template.lt.id }
}
```
li: apply is ~50% done, creating launch template and new instance.
nina: got an alert — aws-node (amazon-vpc-cni) on canary started CrashLoopBackOff after kubelet upgrade. logs: 
```
E0305 09:45:12.123456    1234 cni.go:250] Configure CNI failed: failed to add iptables rule: exec failed: "iptables": executable file not found in $PATH
```
sam: hmm that's odd, iptables missing on the new AMI? did we accidentally switch to a slim image?
li: checking AMI user-data now.
jake: argo reports drift on cluster-config repo — nodegroup launch_template name changed (auto-generated suffix). Argo can't reconcile because k8s node labels differ.
ops-bot: argo-bot: app gpu-cluster detected OutOfSync (resource: NodeGroup/gpu-ng).
li: confirmed AMI build pipeline used base image from infra-images:gpu-2026-03-02 instead of gpu-2026-03-12 (our helper script pointed to the wrong tag). looks like newer AMI is missing iptables package.
nina: we should revert to previous AMI, don't want rollout continuing. CNI needs iptables or nftables compatibility.
sam: can we patch the AMI by installing iptables via user-data and let nodes rejoin? Risky for running pods.
jake: quick mitigation: pause Terraform apply and mark canary nodegroup unschedulable, then roll back LT to previous AMI id.
li: trying to cancel the remaining apply steps — terraform shows "in progress" on instance creation. canceling might leave dangling resources.
ops-bot: terraform: cancel requested by li. status: cancellation in progress.
li: manual patch to node user-data to install iptables and restart kubelet is fastest if we can SSH. but our image disables SSH by default.
nina: cost note — if we spin up replacement nodes in other AZs for safety we'll hit extra spot/ondemand and 20-40% cost delta for the week. flagged to finance. :money_with_wings:
sam: plan: 1) cancel apply 2) lock nodegroup in TF state 3) update launch_template to previous AMI id 4) re-run apply on canary 5) once canary healthy, promote. Thoughts?
jake: +1. also add a post-ami validation script to bake iptables/nftables, cni binary and systemctl status checks — run in image pipeline.
li: taking ownership. I'll rollback LT to ami-0a1b2c3dprev and run a canary apply after cancellation completes.
nina: I'll open an incident page and notify support channel in case customer pods are impacted.
li: ETA 30m to rollback. tagging @sam @jake for visibility.
sam: if rollback fails, fallback: set autoscaler to keep additional on-demand nodes for 2 hours to avoid OOMs.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0318-47 — "canary AMI missing iptables causing CNI crash". responders: nina, li.
li: update: cancellation succeeded, LT rolled back to ami-0a1b2c3dprev, re-applying canary now.
nina: monitoring CNI and kube-proxy logs. so far pods are starting cleanly.
jake: after this we need a gating check in our GitOps pipeline that prevents argo from marking NodeGroup resources OutOfSync when LT name changes — maybe pin launch_template id in repo.
li: opened a PR to infra-images and terraform modules with AMI gating + validation steps. will link in incident.
sam: thanks — keep the channel posted, will stand by for post-mortem and cost estimate. :thumbsup:
li: will post final status in ~1h.
ops-bot: terraform apply completed for canary. new nodes joined and CNI is healthy. canary marked healthy.
